data.final_week_advice: Prioritize timed practice and error analysis in the final weeks, focusing on weak units (4 and 5) and ensuring all topic codes are reviewed.
data.summary: This 10-week plan front-loads the student's weak units (Linear Momentum and Torque) in the first half to allow for repeated review. It integrates live classes into the relevant weeks and concludes with two weeks of mixed review and timed practice to solidify retention before the exam.

weeks.focus: Master foundational kinematics and vector analysis.
tasks: Complete 15 multiple-choice questions on 1D and 2D kinematics, marking each answer with the specific topic code.
Draw and label free-body diagrams for 3 different motion scenarios to reinforce vector concepts.
Review notes on reference frames and relative motion, solving 2 practice problems involving moving observers.

weeks.focus: Build momentum concepts and attend live class on impulse.
tasks: Attend live class #10000 on Linear Momentum and Impulse.
Do 5 free-response questions on conservation of linear momentum, then mark them against the scoring guide.
Calculate impulse for 4 different collision scenarios using the impulse-momentum theorem.

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of collisions and introduce forces.
tasks: Solve 6 problems on elastic and inelastic collisions, tracking kinetic energy changes.
Create free-body diagrams for 5 objects in equilibrium and non-equilibrium states.
Review Newton's Laws by solving 3 problems involving friction and tension.

weeks.focus: Connect work and energy to dynamics.
tasks: Calculate work done by variable forces using graph areas for 3 problems.
Apply conservation of energy to solve 4 problems involving springs and gravity.
Determine power output in 2 mechanical systems, comparing ideal vs. real efficiency.
Attend live class #10001 on Rotational Kinematics and Torque.
Solve 5 problems connecting linear and rotational motion variables.
Calculate net torque and angular acceleration for 3 rigid body systems.

weeks.focus: Integrate rotational energy and angular momentum.
tasks: Compute rotational kinetic energy for 4 different shapes using moment of inertia formulas.
Apply conservation of angular momentum to solve 3 problems involving spinning systems.
Review torque and work relationships by solving 2 combined energy-momentum problems.

weeks.focus: Analyze simple harmonic motion and oscillations.
tasks: Graph position, velocity, and acceleration for 2 SHM systems, labeling key points.
Calculate period and frequency for 4 different oscillators (springs and pendulums).
Solve 3 energy conservation problems for SHM, tracking kinetic and potential energy exchange.
Calculate hydrostatic pressure at various depths in 3 fluid scenarios.
Apply Bernoulli's principle to solve 2 problems involving fluid flow and pressure changes.
Analyze buoyancy by solving 3 problems on floating and sinking objects.

weeks.focus: Mixed review of weak units (Momentum and Rotation).
tasks: Do 10 mixed multiple-choice questions covering Units 4, 5, and 6.
Complete 2 free-response questions on rotational dynamics and angular momentum.
Review error log from previous weeks, re-solving 3 previously missed problems.

weeks.focus: Timed practice and full exam simulation.
tasks: Complete a full 90-minute timed practice exam section covering all units.
Mark the exam using the official scoring guide and identify weak areas.
Solve 5 additional free-response questions on kinematics and energy to reinforce fundamentals.
